From 972787479ee73006fddb5e59ab5c8e733810ff42 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Feng Yang <yangfeng@kylinos.cn>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 17:44:28 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] bpf: test_run: Fix the null pointer dereference issue in
 bpf_lwt_xmit_push_encap

The bpf_lwt_xmit_push_encap helper needs to access skb_dst(skb)->dev to
calculate the needed headroom:

	err = skb_cow_head(skb,
			   len + LL_RESERVED_SPACE(skb_dst(skb)->dev));

But skb->_skb_refdst may not be initialized when the skb is set up by
bpf_prog_test_run_skb function. Executing bpf_lwt_push_ip_encap function
in this scenario will trigger null pointer dereference, causing a kernel
crash as Yinhao reported:

Fixes: 52f278774e79 ("bpf: implement BPF_LWT_ENCAP_IP mode in bpf_lwt_push_encap")
Reported-by: Yinhao Hu <dddddd@hust.edu.cn>
Reported-by: Kaiyan Mei <M202472210@hust.edu.cn>
Closes: https://groups.google.com/g/hust-os-kernel-patches/c/8-a0kPpBW2s
Signed-off-by: Yun Lu <luyun@kylinos.cn>
Signed-off-by: Feng Yang <yangfeng@kylinos.cn>
Signed-off-by: Martin KaFai Lau <martin.lau@kernel.org>
Tested-by: syzbot@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260304094429.168521-2-yangfeng59949@163.com

diff --git a/net/bpf/test_run.c b/net/bpf/test_run.c
index 178c4738e63b..56bc8dc1e281 100644
--- a/net/bpf/test_run.c
+++ b/net/bpf/test_run.c
@@ -1156,6 +1156,21 @@ int bpf_prog_test_run_skb(struct bpf_prog *prog, const union bpf_attr *kattr,
 		skb->ip_summed = CHECKSUM_COMPLETE;
 	}
 
+	if (prog->type == BPF_PROG_TYPE_LWT_XMIT) {
+		if (!ipv6_bpf_stub) {
+			pr_warn_once("Please test this program with the IPv6 module loaded\n");
+			ret = -EOPNOTSUPP;
+			goto out;
+		}
+#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_IPV6)
+		/* For CONFIG_IPV6=n, ipv6_bpf_stub is NULL which is
+		 * handled by the above if statement.
+		 */
+		dst_hold(&net->ipv6.ip6_null_entry->dst);
+		skb_dst_set(skb, &net->ipv6.ip6_null_entry->dst);
+#endif
+	}
+
 	ret = bpf_test_run(prog, skb, repeat, &retval, &duration, false);
 	if (ret)
 		goto out;
-- 
2.34.1

## Patch Summary

This patch fixes a null pointer dereference in the `bpf_lwt_xmit_push_encap` helper when testing `BPF_PROG_TYPE_LWT_XMIT` programs via `bpf_prog_test_run_skb`. The root cause is that `skb_dst(skb)->dev` is accessed without the skb's destination entry being initialized, leading to a crash.

### Modifications in `net/bpf/test_run.c`

- **Added a conditional block** for `BPF_PROG_TYPE_LWT_XMIT` programs before calling `bpf_test_run`.
  - If the IPv6 module is not loaded (`ipv6_bpf_stub` is NULL), the function returns `-EOPNOTSUPP` with a warning.
  - For `CONFIG_IPV6=y`, the code holds a reference to the kernel's IPv6 null entry (`net->ipv6.ip6_null_entry->dst`) and sets it as the skb's destination using `skb_dst_set(skb, ...)`. This ensures `skb_dst(skb)` is non-NULL and has a valid `dev` pointer.

### Relationship

The change directly addresses the null pointer dereference by providing a valid `dst` entry for the `skb` before the test run. The `bpf_lwt_xmit_push_encap` function later calls `skb_dst(skb)->dev`, which would crash if the `dst` is NULL. The fix uses the IPv6 null entry as a safe placeholder, aligning with how LWT XMIT programs expect a valid `dst` during encapsulation operations.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
err = skb_cow_head(skb,
		   len + LL_RESERVED_SPACE(skb_dst(skb)->dev));
```
(inside bpf_lwt_xmit_push_encap)

Reason:
In bpf_prog_test_run_skb, the skb is allocated with `slab_build_skb(data)` but its `_skb_refdst` field is not initialized, so `skb_dst(skb)` returns NULL. When a `BPF_PROG_TYPE_LWT_XMIT` program is tested and calls `bpf_lwt_xmit_push_encap`, it executes the above line, dereferencing `skb_dst(skb)->dev` which is a NULL pointer, causing a kernel crash.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
if (prog->type == BPF_PROG_TYPE_LWT_XMIT) {
		dst_hold(&net->ipv6.ip6_null_entry->dst);
		skb_dst_set(skb, &net->ipv6.ip6_null_entry->dst);
}
```

Reason:
This code sets a valid destination entry for the skb before running the test. It uses the IPv6 null entry (which has a valid `dev`) and holds a reference to it. This ensures that `skb_dst(skb)` is non-NULL when `bpf_lwt_xmit_push_encap` accesses `skb_dst(skb)->dev`, thus preventing the null pointer dereference.
